about.title: ISO 22301:2019 — Business Continuity Management Systems
about.blurb: ISO 22301 specifies the requirements for planning, establishing, implementing, operating, monitoring, reviewing, maintaining, and continually improving a Business Continuity Management System (BCMS). It enables organisations to prepare for, respond to, and recover from disruptive incidents.

p: ISO 22301 follows the Annex SL high-level structure, making it compatible with ISO 27001 and ISO 9001. Clauses 4–10 contain the normative requirements for a BCMS.
The standard applies to organisations of all types and sizes that need to manage the continuity of their critical activities. Certification is available through accredited certification bodies.

groups.name: Context of the Organisation
groups.desc: Clause 4 requires the organisation to understand its context — internal and external issues, interested parties and their requirements, and the scope of the BCMS — before implementing continuity plans.
achieved: Internal and external issues relevant to business continuity are identified and documented.
Interested parties and their continuity-related requirements are identified.
The BCMS scope is formally defined, documented, and approved.
The BCMS is established in the context of the organisation's overall strategic objectives.
evidence: Context analysis document (SWOT/PESTLE or equivalent) (Cl.4.1)
Interested parties register with their BCMS requirements (Cl.4.2)
BCMS Scope Statement with defined boundaries and exclusions (Cl.4.3)

groups.name: Leadership
groups.desc: Clause 5 requires top management to demonstrate commitment to the BCMS through defined leadership behaviours, establishing a business continuity policy, and assigning roles and responsibilities.
achieved: Top management demonstrates active commitment to the BCMS through documented actions.
A business continuity policy is established, approved, communicated, and reviewed.
Roles, responsibilities, and authorities for the BCMS are defined and communicated.
Sufficient resources are allocated to establish, implement, and maintain the BCMS.
evidence: Business Continuity Policy signed by senior management with review history (Cl.5.2)
RACI or organisation chart for BCMS roles and responsibilities (Cl.5.3)
Management review meeting minutes or board papers evidencing commitment (Cl.5.1)

groups.name: Planning
groups.desc: Clause 6 requires the organisation to determine the actions needed to address risks and opportunities, set BCMS objectives, and plan how to achieve them.
achieved: Risks and opportunities relevant to the BCMS are identified and addressed.
Business continuity objectives are established, measurable, and monitored.
Plans to achieve BCMS objectives are documented with owners, timelines, and resources.
Legal and regulatory continuity requirements are identified and addressed.
evidence: BCMS risk and opportunity assessment documentation (Cl.6.1)
Business continuity objectives with measurement criteria and progress tracking (Cl.6.2)
Action plans for achieving BCMS objectives

groups.name: Support
groups.desc: Clause 7 covers the supporting elements of the BCMS — resources, competence, awareness, communication, and documented information — that enable effective implementation.
achieved: Competence requirements for BCMS roles are defined and personnel are suitably qualified or trained.
All relevant personnel are aware of the BC policy, their contribution to the BCMS, and the implications of non-conformity.
Communication procedures for internal and external BC communications are defined.
BCMS documented information is controlled, versioned, and protected.
evidence: BCMS competence requirements and training records (Cl.7.2)
Business continuity awareness training completion records (Cl.7.3)
Communication plan for BCMS-related communications (Cl.7.4)
Document control procedure and BCMS document register (Cl.7.5)

groups.name: Operation
groups.desc: Clause 8 covers the operational requirements of the BCMS — business impact analysis, risk assessment, business continuity strategy, plans, recovery procedures, and exercising. This is where the practical BC capability is built and verified.
achieved: Business Impact Analysis (BIA) determines the impact of disruptions and defines recovery priorities.
BC strategies and solutions address identified recovery requirements.
Business continuity plans are documented and available when needed.
Recovery procedures enable operations to be restored within defined RTOs.
BC plans and procedures are exercised and results are used for improvement.
evidence: Business Impact Analysis (BIA) report with RTO/RPO per activity (Cl.8.2)
Business Continuity Strategy document (Cl.8.3)
Business Continuity Plan(s) with version control (Cl.8.4)
Recovery procedures and runbooks (Cl.8.5)
Exercise programme and exercise reports with improvement actions (Cl.8.6)

items.name: Business Impact Analysis
items.desc: The organisation shall establish, implement, and maintain a formal process to determine the impact of disruptive incidents over time. The BIA identifies time-critical activities, recovery time objectives, recovery point objectives, resource requirements, and dependencies.
achieved: All critical business activities are identified and prioritised.
RTOs and RPOs are defined for each critical activity and validated by business owners.
Resource requirements for recovery (people, technology, facilities) are documented.
Dependencies between activities, suppliers, and systems are mapped.
BIA is reviewed at least annually or when significant changes occur.
evidence: BIA report with critical activity ranking and RTO/RPO per activity
Business owner sign-off on RTO/RPO commitments
Dependency mapping documentation
BIA annual review record

items.name: Business Continuity Strategy
items.desc: Based on the BIA and risk assessment outputs, the organisation shall determine appropriate continuity strategies for protecting prioritised activities, stabilising and continuing those activities, and recovering and restoring them following disruption.
achieved: Continuity strategies are selected for each critical activity based on BIA findings.
Strategies address people, facilities, technology, and information requirements.
Resource requirements for implementing strategies are identified and procured.
Alternate work arrangements (work from home, alternate site) are provisioned.
Strategy selection is reviewed and approved by senior management.
evidence: Business Continuity Strategy document with rationale for strategy choices
Alternate work arrangement documentation
Resource procurement evidence for continuity solutions

items.name: Business Continuity Plans and Procedures
items.desc: The organisation shall document procedures that enable it to manage a disruptive incident and continue critical activities at the required level. Plans must include incident response procedures, activation criteria, communication procedures, and resource management.
achieved: BCP documents are complete, current, and accessible to those who need them.
Plans include clear activation criteria, roles, and communication procedures.
Plans address incidents of varying severity and type.
Plans include procedures for communicating with stakeholders, regulators, and media.
Version control ensures only current plans are used during incidents.
evidence: Business Continuity Plan(s) with version history and approval signatures
Activation criteria and escalation procedures
Stakeholder communication templates

items.name: Recovery
items.desc: The organisation shall have documented procedures for recovering critical activities following a disruption, returning to normal operations, and restoring systems and data within defined recovery objectives.
achieved: Recovery procedures are documented with step-by-step instructions.
Recovery procedures are validated through testing.
IT disaster recovery runbooks are aligned with business recovery plans.
Data restoration procedures meet RPO requirements.
Criteria for returning to normal operations are defined.
evidence: IT disaster recovery runbooks with step-by-step procedures
Recovery test results showing procedures meet RTO/RPO
Return-to-normal operations criteria documentation

items.name: Exercising and Testing
items.desc: The organisation shall exercise and test its business continuity procedures to ensure they are consistent with its business continuity objectives, with exercises conducted at planned intervals and after significant changes.
achieved: An exercise programme is defined covering different exercise types (walkthrough, tabletop, simulation, live).
Exercises are conducted at least annually for critical activities.
Exercise results are documented including objectives met, gaps identified, and improvement actions.
Improvement actions from exercises are tracked to completion.
Exercises involve relevant personnel including senior management.
evidence: Exercise programme document with schedule
Exercise reports with objectives, results, gaps, and improvement actions
Improvement action tracking records showing completion
Senior management participation evidence

groups.name: Performance Evaluation
groups.desc: Clause 9 requires the organisation to monitor, measure, analyse, and evaluate its BCMS to ensure it remains effective, and to conduct internal audits and management reviews.
achieved: BCMS performance metrics are defined and monitored.
Internal audits of the BCMS are conducted at planned intervals.
Top management reviews the BCMS at planned intervals to ensure continued suitability and effectiveness.
Audit findings and performance data are used to drive improvement.
evidence: BCMS performance measurement framework and periodic reports (Cl.9.1)
Internal audit plan, audit records, and findings reports (Cl.9.2)
Management review meeting minutes covering BCMS performance inputs and outputs (Cl.9.3)

groups.name: Improvement
groups.desc: Clause 10 requires the organisation to continually improve the suitability, adequacy, and effectiveness of its BCMS, including through the management of nonconformities and corrective actions.
achieved: Nonconformities are identified, documented, and addressed through root cause analysis.
Corrective actions are implemented and their effectiveness is verified.
The BCMS is continually improved based on findings from audits, exercises, incidents, and management reviews.
Opportunities for improvement are captured and prioritised.
evidence: Nonconformity and corrective action register with root cause analysis records (Cl.10.1)
Evidence of BCMS improvements over successive review periods (Cl.10.2)
Management review decisions including improvement directives (Cl.9.3 output)
